[footBayes]{.fb-title}

[`footBayes` is an R package for the estimation, visualization and prediction of goal-based football models: double Poisson, bivariate Poisson, Dixon-Coles, negative binomial, Skellam, Student-$t$, diagonal-inflated bivariate Poisson and zero-inflated Skellam. Models are fitted by maximum likelihood or in a Bayesian framework through Stan, with static or dynamic team abilities.]{.fb-lead}

::: {.fb-section .column-page}
## Key features

- **Goal-based models**: double Poisson, bivariate Poisson, Dixon-Coles, negative binomial, Skellam, Student-$t$, diagonal-inflated bivariate Poisson and zero-inflated Skellam ([Goal-based models in a nutshell](articles/goal-based-models.qmd)).
- **Inference**: maximum likelihood with `mle_foot()`, or Bayesian inference with `stan_foot()` through HMC, Pathfinder, ADVI and the Laplace approximation ([Static models](articles/static-models.qmd)).
- **Dynamic abilities**: weekly or seasonal team abilities, with common variance, variance inflation after the summer break, or weighted dynamic models with commensurate priors ([Dynamic models](articles/dynamic-models.qmd)).
- **Checks, predictions and comparison**: posterior predictive checks, match probabilities, league table reconstruction and model comparison through predictive metrics ([Predictions](articles/predictions.qmd)).
:::

::: {.fb-section .column-page}
## Installation

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
`footBayes` requires the R package [`cmdstanr`](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/) (not on CRAN) and [CmdStan](https://mc-stan.org/users/interfaces/cmdstan.html). For a step-by-step installation, follow [Getting started with CmdStanR](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/articles/cmdstanr.html).
:::

::: {.fb-install-grid}
::: {.fb-install-box}
#### Released version (CRAN)

```r
install.packages("footBayes", type = "source")
```

Setting `type = "source"` is important: otherwise the CmdStan models in the package may not be compiled during installation.
:::

::: {.fb-install-box}
#### Development version (GitHub)

```r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("leoegidi/footBayes")
```
:::
:::
:::

::: {.fb-section .column-page}
## A quick example

Fit a Bayesian double Poisson model to the Italian Serie A (seasons 2000/2001 to 2002/2003) and predict the last four match days of the 2002/2003 season:

```r
library(footBayes)
library(dplyr)

data("italy")
italy_2000_2002 <- italy %>%
  dplyr::select(Season, home, visitor, hgoal, vgoal) %>%
  filter(Season %in% c("2000", "2001", "2002"))

colnames(italy_2000_2002) <- c("periods", "home_team", "away_team",
                               "home_goals", "away_goals")

fit1 <- stan_foot(data = italy_2000_2002,
                  model = "double_pois",
                  predict = 36,
                  iter_sampling = 200,
                  chains = 2)

print(fit1, pars = c("att", "def"))
```

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Abilities

```r
foot_abilities(fit1, italy_2000_2002)
```

![](images/readme_foot_abilities.png){fig-alt="Posterior attack and defence abilities of the Serie A teams"}

### Model checks

```r
pp_foot(fit1, italy_2000_2002)
```

![](images/readme_pp_foot.png){fig-alt="Posterior predictive check of the goal differences"}

### League table

```r
foot_rank(fit1, italy_2000_2002)
```

![](images/readme_foot_rank.png){fig-alt="Observed and predicted final points of each team"}

### Match probabilities

```r
foot_prob(fit1, italy_2000_2002)
```

![](images/readme_foot_prob.png){fig-alt="Home win, draw and away win probabilities of the predicted matches"}
